e.etymology: A respelling of Kaden, also written Caden, one of the rhyming names (Aiden, Jayden, Brayden) that swept the United States in the 2000s.

e.meaning: he shines (as a form of Jair)
e.etymology: In Latin America a spelling of Jair, the biblical Hebrew Yair, he shines or he enlightens. In South Asia Jahir is a separate name, a form of Arabic Zahir, evident or manifest.
A respelling of Hudson, an English surname meaning son of Hudd, a medieval pet form of Hugh and Richard. The -syn ending, as in Emersyn, is used for girls and boys alike.

assoc.t: Hudson River and Hudson Bay (spelled Hudson)

e.etymology: A phonetic spelling in the family of Kailani and Kehlani. Kailani is Hawaiian, from kai, sea, and lani, sky or heaven; the kay sound follows the singer Kehlani.

assoc.t: Kehlani, R&B singer (same sound)

e.etymology: A modern elaboration of Kay or Kayla with the -leen ending of Colleen, Eileen and Kathleen. It belongs to the same family as Kaylin and Kaylene.
A spelling of Drew, the short form of Andrew, from Greek andreios, manly. For girls it has also been a short form of Drusilla.

assoc.t: Gru's twin brother in Despicable Me 3

e.etymology: From Arabic Adnan, settler, from a root meaning to stay or abide. In Arab tradition Adnan was the ancestor of the northern Arab tribes and a forefather of the Prophet Muhammad.
namesakes: Adnan Syed (subject of the Serial podcast)

e.etymology: An elaboration of Angel and Angela used mostly in Spanish-speaking families, especially in the Caribbean. The root is Greek angelos, messenger.
A modern name in the family of Daylin, Dalen and Jaylin, built from the Day- sound and the popular -lyn ending. It has no older meaning of its own.
A respelling of Easton, an English surname and place name from Old English east and tun, the settlement to the east.
From Arabic sanad, a support or prop. The same word names the chain of authorities that backs up a hadith.
Transferred from the English surname, probably a variant of Tenley, which began as a place name. It caught on in the 2010s alongside Tenley, Finley and Kinley.

assoc.t: Tinley Park, a Chicago suburb

e.meaning: born of Ra, the sun god
e.etymology: From Egyptian ra-mes-su, Ra is the one who bore him, through Greek Rhamesses. Eleven pharaohs bore the name, the best known being Ramses II, called the Great.
namesakes: Ramses II (pharaoh of Egypt known as Ramses the Great)

assoc.t: Ramses II, the best-known pharaoh of ancient Egypt

e.etymology: A spelling of Eleanor, from the medieval Occitan name Alienor, whose origin is uncertain. Tolkien also made Elanor, sun-star in his Elvish language, a golden flower and the name of Sam Gamgee's daughter.

assoc.t: Sam Gamgee's daughter in The Lord of the Rings

e.etymology: The English form of Phinehas, a priest and grandson of Aaron in the Hebrew Bible; the Hebrew Pinchas probably comes from Egyptian pa-nehasi, the Nubian. Phineus is also a blind seer in Greek myth.
namesakes: Phineas Flynn (inventor stepbrother of Disney's Phineas and Ferb)
P. T. Barnum (circus showman, born Phineas Taylor Barnum)
Phineas Gage (railroad worker whose brain injury is a classic case study)

assoc.t: Phineas of Disney's cartoon Phineas and Ferb

e.etymology: From the English word coral, which comes from Latin corallium and Greek korallion. It came into fashion in the late 1800s with other gemstone names for girls.

assoc.t: reef-building sea animal and the gem made from it
pinkish-orange color
Nemo's mother in Finding Nemo

e.etymology: A modern American name that rose in the early 2000s alongside Amaya, Amiyah and Aniya. It is usually treated as a spelling of one of those and has no settled meaning of its own.
As a Jewish given name, the Yiddish form of Hebrew Meir, one who gives light. As a surname it is also German, from Meier, the steward or leaseholder of a manor.
namesakes: Meyer Lansky (organized-crime figure known as the Mob's Accountant)

assoc.t: Meyer lemon, a sweet thin-skinned lemon
Mrs. Meyer's Clean Day household cleaners

e.etymology: A Latin American spelling of Diana that follows the English pronunciation. Diana was the Roman goddess of the hunt and the moon; her name goes back to a root meaning sky or divine.
The English spelling of German Hänsel, little Hans, a pet form of Johannes (John), from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious.
namesakes: Hansel (boy in the Grimm fairy tale Hansel and Gretel)
Hansel (Owen Wilson's rival model in Zoolander)

assoc.t: boy in the Grimm fairy tale Hansel and Gretel
Owen Wilson's model in Zoolander

e.note: Nearly everyone will think of Hansel and Gretel on hearing the name.

e.etymology: A pet form of Lon and Alonzo. Alonzo is a form of Alfonso, a Germanic name brought to Spain by the Visigoths and built from words for noble and ready.

e.meaning: of Elysium, the paradise of Greek myth
e.etymology: From Elysium, the blessed fields where heroes rested in Greek myth; Elysia is the Latin feminine form of the adjective. Some parents also treat it as an elaboration of Elise or Alyssa.
The Catalan short form of Xavier, from the Navarrese place name Xabier, Basque etxe berri, new house. Saint Francis Xavier turned the place name into a given name.
namesakes: Xavi Hernandez (Spanish soccer midfielder and former Barcelona coach)

assoc.t: Spanish soccer great Xavi, known by the one name

e.note: Said SHAH-vee in Catalan and often HAH-vee in Spanish; Americans may guess ZAY-vee or ZAH-vee.

e.etymology: A modern American coinage, a spelling of Kyson, which joins the Ky- of Kyle and Kyler to the -son ending of Tyson and Bryson.
From a Germanic name built from arn, eagle, and wald, power or rule. The Normans brought it to England, and it had a second run of popularity in the late 1800s and early 1900s.
namesakes: Arnold Schwarzenegger (action star and former governor of California)
Arnold Shortman (football-headed kid of Nickelodeon's Hey Arnold!)

assoc.t: Arnold Schwarzenegger, often called just Arnold
title kid of Nickelodeon's Hey Arnold!
Arnold sandwich bread

e.etymology: A modern spelling of Aubrey, the Norman French form of the Germanic name Alberic, from alb, elf, and ric, ruler. Aubrey was mostly a man's name until the late 20th century.
From Turkish demir, iron, a name that wishes a boy strength. It is also a common Turkish surname and is used in Albania and Bosnia.

e.meaning: from Kent, the English county whose name means rim or border
e.etymology: From the surname for someone from Kent, the county in southeast England. Its name goes back through Latin Cantium to a Celtic word for a corner or rim, fitting land at the coast.
namesakes: Kent Brockman (news anchor on The Simpsons)

assoc.t: Clark Kent, Superman's everyday identity
county in southeast England
Kent cigarettes

e.etymology: A K spelling of Carmen, from the Spanish title of Mary as Our Lady of Mount Carmel; Hebrew karmel means garden or orchard. Karmen is the usual spelling in Slovenia, Croatia and Estonia.
From Irish Éamonn, the Irish form of Edmund, which comes from Old English ead, prosperity, and mund, protector.
namesakes: Eamon de Valera (Irish revolutionary leader and president)
e.note: Often misread as EE-mun or ee-AH-mon; the Irish pronunciation is AY-mun.

e.etymology: A 19th-century variant of Lulu, the pet name for Louisa and Lucy, and occasionally short for Tallulah. It was common for American girls in the late 1800s.
namesakes: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva (president of Brazil, known as Lula)

assoc.t: Lula, the president of Brazil

e.etymology: A variant of Audrey, from Old English Æthelthryth, noble strength. It rose after the character Audra Barkley on the 1960s western The Big Valley. Lithuanian Audra is a separate name meaning storm.
namesakes: Audra McDonald (Broadway star with six Tony Awards)
